articles.title: Fire flares up again at Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat in Bavarian Alps
articles.summary: Fire erupted again overnight at the Eagle's Nest mountain retreat in southern Germany that was once used by Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler, Bavarian police repor...
articles.body:
Fire erupted again overnight at the Eagle's Nest mountain retreat in southern Germany that was once used by Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler, Bavarian police reported on Sunday.

"It was burning up to room height again," a police officer said.

Firefighters were dispatched to the historic site, known as Kehlsteinhaus in German, atop the Obersalzberg peak and extinguished the flames. It is not unusual for a fire to flare up again because of smouldering embers after the main blaze has been extinguished, the officer added.

A major fire broke out at Eagle's Nest on Friday evening. Police arrested a suspect on suspicion of arson.

An initial psychiatric assessment of the 33-year-old German man concluded that he was mentally ill, according to prosecutors.

The building was largely destroyed by the blaze, with the damage estimated to amount to millions of euros.

Eagle's Nest, situated at an altitude of more than 1,800 metres, was built under the Nazi regime in the 1930s as part of the complex used by Hitler on the Obersalzberg.

It has been used as a restaurant since 1952. However, the establishment was closed on Friday and no one was injured in the blaze.

Hitler visited Eagle's Nest several times to receive diplomats and other foreign guests, according to the local tourism association in Berchtesgaden.

However, politically, the retreat "remained of little significance" and was mainly used by senior Nazi officials for leisure purposes and private celebrations, according to the association.

Today, it houses an exhibition highlighting its Nazi history.

articles.title: Class 11 student abducted, raped and murdered in West Bengal's Gaighata, 1 held
articles.summary: 17-year-old Class 11 student abducted, raped and murdered in Gaighata, North 24 Parganas; body found Sunday; 23-year-old Prahlad Das arrested; SIT formed.
articles.body: KOLKATA: A 17-year-old girl, a student of Class 11, was allegedly abducted, raped and murdered near the Indo-Bangladesh border at Gaighata, North 24 Parganas, on Saturday night.Her naked body was recovered from behind a neighbour’s house on Sunday morning, triggering protests in the area.Police arrested Prahlad Das, 23, a resident of Shimulpur in Gaighata and said to have been known to the victim.A Bongaon court remanded him in 10 days of police custody on Sunday afternoon.According to police, the girl had attended a soiree near her house on Saturday night. Her family alleged she received a phone call around 11.30pm and left the event.When she did not return, family relatives, and neighbours searched for her through the night. Her body, bearing multiple injuries, was recovered in the morning.Her aunt said she had last seen the girl on Saturday evening. “She told us she was going to the jalsa with a friend. In the morning, we heard about this horrific incident,” she said.Bongaon Police District SP Bidisha Kalita Dasgupta said a rape and murder case had been registered based on the family’s complaint.A special investigation team headed by the ASP of Bongaon has been formed. A medical board has been constituted for the post-mortem, which will be videographed. A forensic team has been called to collect evidence from the crime scene.“We are investigating whether more people were involved. The accused will be interrogated further,” the SP said.Preliminary questioning has indicated the accused allegedly harboured resentment against the girl over remarks she had made about his mother. Investigators are examining the motive and whether others were involved.A large police contingent including RAF and Combat Force personnel was deployed to bring the situation under control following protests by local residents.Gaighata MLA Subrata Thakur condemned the incident and said his party stood by the victim’s family, demanding the harshest possible punishment.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Land, money dispute, broken marriage alliance behind Bengaluru battery IED blast; 3 held
articles.summary: Bengaluru IED blast: Police arrest 3 over torch-battery parcel explosion in Frazer Town; land, money and broken marriage alliance cited as motive.
articles.body: BENGALURU:A parcel containing an improvised explosive device (IED) concealed inside a torch battery turned into a deadly trap for two workers at an under-construction building on Jeremaiah Road in Frazer Town.Police suspect the blast was part of a premeditated murder plot stemming from a land dispute, financial disagreements and a broken marriage alliance.East Division police have arrested three persons, Bhurhan Ahmad Burbhuiyya, 20, who works as a welder and electrician in Maski, Raichur district; Jahidull Hussain Burbhuiyya, 27, a salesman at a bakery in Jayanagar; and Sajidull Lashkar, 22, who works in the kitchen of a restaurant in Malleswaram.All three are natives of Dinanathpur in Hailakandi district of Assam.Two persons were injured in the incident: Allauddin, from Dinanathpur and a relative of Jahidull, and Sajidull, a childhood friend of Bhurhan and Jahidull.Both worked at the under-construction building, with duties including painting and security. Allauddin and Jahidull had financial, property and personal issues involving their families.The explosion occurred on October 20 at a building under construction within the jurisdiction of Pulakeshinagar police station.Two workers, Suraj and Allauddin, sustained serious injuries in the blast. Allauddin was later discharged from hospital after receiving treatment.According to police, a painter lodged a complaint after a loud explosion rocked the building’s fifth floor while workers were on duty.A preliminary inspection revealed that an improvised explosive device (IED), concealed inside a torch battery, had detonated, injuring the two workers.Taking the case seriously, deputy commissioner of police (East) Vikram Amathe formed 10 special teams to investigate the incident from multiple angles.Investigators analysed footage from more than 1,500 CCTV cameras and questioned over 100 people as part of the probe. Their efforts led to the arrest of two suspects in Bengaluru. A third accused was subsequently apprehended in Maski and brought in for questioning.During interrogation, police learnt that the three accused were childhood friends of Allauddin who conspired to commit the crime and shared information through a WhatsApp group.The injured worker and all three accused are neighbours.Police said the prime accused, Jahidull, is a cousin of the injured Allauddin.The two had a strained relationship over a land dispute and financial differences in their native village. An issue involving the cancellation of Jahidull’s sister’s marriage is also suspected to have added to the animosity.According to investigators, Jahidull plotted to kill Allauddin and enlisted the help of the other two accused. The trio gathered information through online web applications, purchased raw materials locally and assembled the IED themselves after searching for information about it online.As part of the plan, they concealed the device inside a torch battery, packed it in a parcel and left it at a petty shop near the building, ensuring that the intended target would collect it. Accused Bhurhan then pressured Allauddin on the phone to open the parcel.However, the plan resulted in coworker Suraj opening the parcel.The accused spoke in Hindi, and Allauddin claimed that he did not understand Hindi, triggering the explosion. Suraj, who opened it, suffered serious injuries and is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital.Police said the three accused were produced before a court and taken into police custody for detailed interrogation. The three arrested men have no criminal background.Questioning is continuing to ascertain where they procured the explosives, and further investigation is under way to establish all the circumstances surrounding the conspiracy and the blast and determine whether the UAPA needs to be invoked in the case.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Delhi Police register case over Jamia Campus trespassing, defacement
articles.summary: Delhi Police file FIR over alleged unauthorised entry and defacement at Jamia amid 14-day student union election protest; campus shifted online, security tight.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Hundreds of students and alumni gathered at Jamia Millia Islamia Sunday as the agitation demanding the restoration of students’ union elections entered its 14th day. The demonstration continued despite the university’s decision Saturday to shift classes online and close campus gates and libraries until further notice.With police personnel deployed in large numbers and barricades erected outside the university, students reportedly made their way through different entrances to reach the protest site near Gate No. 7. Demonstrators raised slogans, displayed placards and demanded that the gates be reopened to allow others to join the protest. According to some students, the university vice-chancellor, along with some other university members, visited the protest site around noon but left without engaging with the demonstrators.Delhi Police, meanwhile, registered a case on a complaint from the university administration after several individuals allegedly entered the campus without authorisation on Friday. Two MPs and other individuals not associated with Jamia allegedly entered the campus, triggering chaos and tension on the university premises. Police intervened and some of those involved were detained. No one was named as a suspect in the FIR. One person was detained Sunday in connection with the alleged trespassing.Police also added a section related to defacement after “objectionable” slogans and graffiti appeared on the university walls, sources confirmed. The graffiti included messages, such as “Free Kashmir” and “Free Sharjeel Imam”, along with slogans targeting the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Protesters have denied responsibility for the graffiti.Police are scanning CCTV footage from the university campus and surrounding areas to identify those allegedly involved in the defacement. Investigators are examining the footage and other evidence to establish the sequence of events and ascertain who was responsible. The investigation into the alleged trespassing and defacement is ongoing.Security remained heightened outside the university campus as a precautionary measure to prevent any untoward incident and maintain law and order amid the prevailing tension.The agitation began on Oct 12, with students sitting on a protest and hunger strike demanding the restoration of the university’s students’ union and elections.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Man killed as Mercedes driven by judge’s minor son hits scooter in Keralam
articles.summary: Kochi: 55-year-old scooter rider killed after Mercedes driven by 17-year-old judge’s son hit from behind; FIR filed, more charges likely, juvenile action awaited.
articles.body: KOCHI: A Mercedes-Benz driven by a 17-year-old son of an additional sessions judge rammed into a scooter on Container Road near Maraparamb in Cheranelloor here around 2.20am on Sunday, killing a 55-year-old man.The deceased was identified as Jayabalakrishnan, son of Rangaswamy Chettiyar of South Chittoor.He ran a roadside eatery and was reportedly heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery, and a preliminary police investigation indicated that the car hit the scooter from behind.An FIR has been registered under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for rash driving and causing death by negligence. Police later said Section 105, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, would be added following allegations that no strong action was being taken in the case.The 17-year-old was released from the police station earlier as the offences initially invoked were bailable. Police sources said a decision on further action, including apprehending him and producing him before the Juvenile Justice Board, would be taken soon.A senior officer with Cheranelloor police said the minor underwent a medical examination, and the preliminary report indicated that he had not consumed alcohol. A detailed report is awaited. A preliminary investigation indicated that the boy was alone in the car, the officer said.Meanwhile, Jayalakshmi, a relative of the victim, described the accident scene as horrifying. “One of his footwear items was on the road, while the other chappal and helmet were some distance away on the service road. The damage to the vehicles itself showed the intensity of the collision,” she told reporters.She alleged that the minor’s father told her not to question him when she asked why a minor had been allowed to drive. She said she insisted on meeting the boy’s parents after police personnel told her that his father was a judicial officer.Police have not revealed the minor’s details since Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act prohibits the disclosure of the identity or any other particulars that may lead to the identification of a child in conflict with the law.Police said the teen claimed that the scooter suddenly swerved to avoid waterlogging and he couldn’t stop on time to avoid the collision. There was heavy rain during the early hours on Sunday.The accident comes close on the heels of another high-profile accident here on Oct 11, when a Mini Cooper car driven by a 19-year-old mowed down a scooter, killing three youths. Suhail (19), who was behind the wheel, was inebriated and the car was driven at an extreme speed. He is still in remand. Police later found that the accused had consumed liquor from three different bar hotels before the accident.Meanwhile, Youth Congress leader Shajahan P Y lodged a complaint with home minister Ramesh Chennithala, seeking strong action under Section 119A of the Motor Vehicles Act. The provision holds the guardian of a juvenile or the owner of the vehicle guilty of the contravention in such situations and liable to be proceeded against.However, the guardian or owner will not be liable to punishment if they prove that the offence was committed without their knowledge or that they exercised due diligence to prevent it. articles.title: Pune police write to Google & Apple to take down Rapido from their app stores
articles.summary: Pune police ask Google and Apple to remove Rapido for alleged unauthorised bike taxis; FIR filed, approvals pending as riders and unions debate safety and access.
articles.body: Pune: City police, in their efforts to remove bike taxi option from Rapido’s app, reached out to Google and Apple.The move follows last week’s letter from Pune Collector and Regional Transport Authority chairperson Jitendra Dudi, asking police to shut down the bike taxi service.Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the police have written to Google and Apple. “We have already sent communications to Google Play Store and Apple’s App Store to put down Rapido’s application,” he told TOI.Pune RTO officials said the service could soon become unavailable unless Rapido secures the necessary approvals. The company’s application seeking approval to operate bike taxis has been pending with the transport department. “They were warned of legal action if they failed to comply with the norms. An FIR was lodged against them last week, and now the RTA chairperson and police have also stepped in,” an RTO official said, requesting anonymity.“If they comply with all requirements under the bike taxi policy, they may get approval. However, their unauthorised operations could complicate matters,” the official said.The bike taxi option remains active on the Rapido app and rides continue across the city despite an FIR being registered against it more than a week ago. Some commuters have questioned the authorities’ push to shut down the service, arguing that public transport remains inadequate and that passengers continue to face overcharging and misbehaviour by some autorickshaw and cab drivers.“I don’t understand why the authorities are so keen to close the service. They cannot ensure adequate public transport and do little when cabbies and autorickshaw drivers overcharge or misbehave. I used the [Rapido bike taxi] service a couple of days ago and found it perfectly fine,” said a Vimannagar resident on the condition of anonymity.Inder Rastogi, a young working professional and friend of the Vimannagar resident, said authorities should focus on regulating the service and improving safety rather than shutting it down. “One of the friends lives in Hinjewadi Phase III and has been watching empty Metro trains run for over a month. The govt has been waiting for the PM to inaugurate the service, with no clarity on when it would begin. Authorities could make bike taxis safer instead of trying to shut them down. The service operates successfully in several cities. They are buckling under pressure from autorickshaw unions,” he said.Autorickshaw unions, meanwhile, criticised the authorities for issuing letters without ensuring that operations cease. They also raised concerns about the verification of riders and passenger safety. “Only a few days ago, the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad caught a bike taxi operator who allegedly had links with a terrorist organisation in Pakistan. It is high time the service was stopped,” said Keshav Kshirsagar, president of Maharashtra Kamgar Sabha and Indian Gig Workers Front.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: Peru, Chile, Bolívia, Paraguai: líderes da direita parabenizam Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: O petista derrotou Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e se tornou o primeiro presidente da história do Brasil a ser eleito quatro vezes pelo voto popular.
articles.summary: O petista derrotou Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e se tornou o primeiro presidente da história do Brasil a ser eleito quatro vezes pelo voto popular.
articles.body:
Presidentes de direita da América Latina parabenizaram neste domingo (25) Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) pela reeleição à Presidência do Brasil.

Entre eles estão os presidentes do Chile , José Antonio Kast, do Paraguai , Santiago Peña , e da Bolívia , Rodrigo Paz . Eles foram eleitos na chamada " onda azul ", que elegeu líderes conservadores em vários países do continente .

Outros representantes da guinada à direira, como o argentino Javier Milei e o colombiano Abelardo de la Espriella, ainda não haviam se manifestado até a última atualização desta reportagem. O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , que encabeça o movimento, também não havia se manifestado.

As manifestações destacaram a disposição de manter a cooperação com o Brasil em áreas como integração econômica, segurança e desenvolvimento regional, apesar das diferenças ideológicas entre os governos.

Às vésperas de completar 81 anos, o que ocorrerá na próxima terça-feira (27), o petista se tornou, ao derrotar Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), o primeiro presidente da história do Brasil a ser eleito quatro vezes pelo voto popular.

O equatoriano Daniel Noboa parabenizou Lula pela vitória e afirmou que a América Latina tem inimigos em comum e desafios compartilhados. Ele defendeu a cooperação entre os países da região e disse que há muito a ganhar com o trabalho conjunto.

O chileno Kast afirmou que conversou com Lula e o parabenizou pelo resultado da eleição. O presidente chileno disse que os dois países têm um futuro em comum e defendeu o fortalecimento das relações bilaterais, com foco na integração econômica e no combate ao crime organizado na região.

Peña, que lidera o Paraguai, também felicitou Lula e afirmou que Paraguai e Brasil compartilham uma agenda de integração e desenvolvimento. Segundo ele, os dois governos continuarão trabalhando juntos pelo bem-estar de suas populações.

O líder boliviano, Rodrigo Paz, por sua vez, parabenizou o presidente brasileiro pela vitória e destacou os laços históricos e os desafios compartilhados entre Bolívia e Brasil. O presidente boliviano afirmou que pretende manter a cooperação bilateral para fortalecer as relações entre os países e ampliar oportunidades para suas populações.

A presidente do Peru , Keiko Fujimori , também felicitou Lula e o povo brasileiro pela jornada democrática. Ela defendeu o fortalecimento da aliança estratégica entre os dois países, com ênfase na integração, na cooperação e no desenvolvimento sustentável da Amazônia compartilhada.

articles.title: Healey’s Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds
articles.summary: The economic is positive now but come January things could become trickier for the Labour government
articles.body:
The chancellor's aides are using intelligence-style security measures to guard its secrets: the Budget has been split into "compartments" with very few given access to all of them. There are codenames. The IT has been locked down and ministers viewing the plans have to sign a digital promise not to brief media.

Such security is a response to the feeling that speculation around the last Budget, sometimes informed by insiders, was economically destabilising.

As a recent former defence secretary, Chancellor John Healey has embraced such strict procedures, and has approached most of his public engagements and interviews with a sturdy refusal to break the Budget omertà, akin to his fellow Yorkshireman Geoffrey Boycott's at times ultra-defensive stance on a cricket pitch.

The economic news has been good - growth has been better than expected and the International Monetary Fund has endorsed the UK for "standing out" among the G7 countries for at least planning to cut borrowing.

The bond market's reverse beauty contest, in which investors single out the countries they distrust most, has moved on from Britain. Traders I occasionally hear from who were once focused on UK borrowing costs are now more preoccupied with "le spread" - the widening gap between French and German borrowing costs (the former being higher than the latter) - and with America's long-term debt outlook.

And yet there are clouds on the horizon. The inflation rate rose more than forecast to 3.5% in September, and borrowing numbers were also higher than forecast. This means an imminent Bank of England rate rise is very much on the cards, with the resultant rise in mortgage repayments for some.

Credibility with investors requires not just that Budget maths add up on Wednesday, but also belief that growth plans are realistic, and the perception that Downing Street can actually convince MPs to pass its Budget.

The question for John Healey is whether he can deliver a Budget that can sustain the revival in growth and offer the help with the cost of living that his backbenchers demand. At the same time he needs to reassure the markets that his budget will keep a check on borrowing.

"Is it resilient, or is it actually strong?" has been the tone of the debate among economists about the curious case of the UK economy ahead what is a vital Budget.

The UK is the fastest growing G7 country so far this year, at 0.6% in Q1 and 0.5% in Q2. The widespread assumption of stagnation in the second half is being defied with Q3 heading for 0.6 to 0.8%.

Each quarter has seen growth twice as fast as predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March and independent forecasters. This is the fastest growth in the first eight months of a year since 2017, ignoring the post-lockdown re-opening.

It's more resilient than it was in 2022. Back then, the Ukraine war, massive energy bailouts, and Liz Truss' mini budget all culminated in the UK facing the highest borrowing costs in the G7, in what was derided in financial markets as a "moron premium".

Then last year, with constant policy u-turns, UK borrowing costs rose the most of the G7.

This year the gap has narrowed, as uncertainty about the US and France takes centre stage, but all advanced economies are feeling the heat from the Iran war energy shock.

Inflation has risen, but not just in Britain. The link between gas and electricity prices has weakened, meaning spikes in gas prices have less impact on electricity bills than they used to and helping to keep inflation lower than it otherwise might have been.

The fact that up until now the Iran war has been more of an oil shock than a gas shock (where the UK is more exposed) has been another saving grace. Meanwhile, the significant amount of AI and tech investment in the UK is another boost to the economic numbers.

The net result is that doom-mongering predictions of recession, of being hit worst by the Iran war, and, in some quarters, of imminent national bankruptcy, have been defied.

That economic defiance of the early part of 2026 has persisted in the first three months of the Burnham-Healey tenure in Downing Street, buoyed by a lull in the Iran war and the energy price shock.

Burnham was advised upon entry to Downing Street that if consumers could at least feel more confident, they might save less and spend more and therefore help boost growth.

So far Burnham and Healey appear to be relying on a series of relatively inexpensive "feel-better" policies - such as capped bus fares and a temporary VAT cut on household energy bills - that have improved confidence without significantly increasing spending.

But there isn't a lot of spare money, which limits just how much can be offered for "temporary and targeted" measures. And come January, the clouds on the horizon could be overhead, with typical energy bills predicted to rise by 16%, interest rates potentially up and an enduring fear that the AI bubble could burst.

At a gleaming hi-tech robotics research facility in Coventry last month, John Healey sought to set out the broad contours of his approach to the economy. On a walkabout at the Manufacturing Technology Centre, I asked him if there had been too much doom-mongery.

"I know the global conditions mean that it is hard… we have huge latent potential in this country. Great talent, and deep capital markets.

"The challenge now is to make sure that we balance the books, we manage and control public spending, and the prime minister and I are in lockstep in our determination to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer," he said.

The giant orange robot arms whizzing around were being trained by AI to use lasers to carve the most intricate metal shapes for prototype parts for the jet engines of the future. The Budget manoeuvres required by Healey may require even more precision.

The essential question is whether he has chosen to impress the markets and explain himself to his MPs, or impress his MPs and explain himself to the markets. Judging by my three interviews with him in recent weeks, it is more the former than the latter.

The answer may not be found in his speech at all, but in the borrowing tables that will reveal how much money the government expects to borrow over the coming years, published in the OBR's forecast released - assuming no repeat of last year's disaster - when Healey sits down in the House of Commons around 13.00.

Just after that, as Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch is delivering the Opposition's response, the real reaction the chancellor's team will be looking for is whether the markets move, particularly when the Debt Management Office publishes the "gilt remit" - the detail of any changes to its plan to sell UK government bonds to investors.

My sense is that every effort is being made to minimise this number, and help guide down medium and long-term borrowing rates for the government and for mortgages. (It was at this moment in 2022 that markets vomited at the prospect of how much extra they thought the government would need to borrow after Liz Truss' mini budget.)

From Healey's first day in office, the prudence message was practically tattooed to his head. He has spent more time working in the Treasury than any recent chancellor. He spent five years from 2002 to 2007 as a junior minister when Gordon Brown was chancellor - five finance bills, five Budgets, pre-Budget reports and two Spending Reviews.

For his Labour Party conference speech, Healey sported Brown's old conference tie. But the Treasury he returned to this year is a changed place in important ways. When his predecessor wore the tie, the Treasury was running an annual surplus, not a £120bn deficit adding to a £3 trillion total national debt.

I asked him just afterwards, and just before he was whisked off to a meeting of the government's emergency COBR committee on RAF Fairford, if he was going to have another go at some of the things that proved so difficult for his predecessor, former Chancellor Rachel Reeves.

He replied: "100%. I was very clear to the conference today and the public beyond. There isn't the money that there was in the 1990s. People understand that. The public aren't daft.

"Running through the Budget I deliver must be fiscal discipline and the maintenance of control on the public finances, because otherwise we won't get on top of the debt costs."

One intriguing element of what we may see on Wednesday is that this theoretically more left-leaning Labour government appears to believe they have the political capital to save money on welfare payments.

The aim is to get some of the 1.35 million people currently off work with mental health issues back into jobs.

Some reporting suggests some affected younger people may see benefits payments cut, with the government instead investing more in getting them into jobs and keeping them in them through the offer, for example, of in-work therapy.

Back in Healey's time under Gordon Brown, there was no OBR. Back then it was not unknown for late budget maths problems to be settled with an optimistic tweak of a forecast, a date change to the economic cycle, or choosing a stronger rate of long term growth.

The OBR's verdict is crucial now - to what extent it agrees with projected welfare savings or even the importance it places on stronger GDP figures matters now.

The bigger point here is that the chancellor must be shocked by the contrast between the sheer power of the Brown Treasury to do what it wanted, and the reality of what he currently faces: the constraints of the OBR, manifesto red lines, bond markets, significant debts and an energy shock.

There are reasons to postpone some of the toughest decisions beyond this Budget, such as how to fund desired increases in spending on defence and social care. The economic outlook could improve were the Iran war to settle at some point in the next few months, and after revised statistics the OBR may also have cause to rethink last year's downgrade to long term economic growth.

There is an imaginable pathway to a forecast next year with higher growth, lower inflation and lower debt interest costs, plausibly improving the public finance projections by tens of billions.

This would be a much more agreeable basis upon which to decide the pace of those big ticket spending rises. It also may be a tempting option for anyone thinking about an election. Former Treasury officials lament: "There is always a reason for procrastination."

Expect the Chancellor to laud the resilience and strength of the UK economy and seek to sustain it, and spread growth geographically. His key judgement, however, will be a balance between extra financial and economic support and the peril of still elevated borrowing costs.

He will try to offer breathing space. It may be needed not just for households and families, but for the Exchequer itself.

articles.title: Serbia's student movement: How and why students brought down Vučić
articles.summary: In just under two years the students have succeeded in tearing up 14 years of political dominance under Aleksandar Vučić.
articles.body:
Theirs is a movement born from tragedy that began with students blockading streets and turned into almost daily protests and a national movement against corruption and government negligence.

In just under two years the students have succeeded in tearing up 14 years of political dominance under Aleksandar Vučić, who has seen support for his Serbian Progressive party (SNS) ebb away and ultimately fail in what became a referendum on the future of Serbia.

From Belgrade to Novi Sad and Niš, the mood was euphoric as supporters gathered in town centres or in front of Student List headquarters. In a post on social media, the students declared "Serbia is free".

Most symbolic of all was the demise of so-called Ćaciland, a pro-Vučić tent camp set up 18 months ago at Pioneers Park in central Belgrade in front of the Serbian parliament. Metal fences were torn down amid shouts of "Vučić is leaving".

They have no obvious leaders and have no grounding in politics, and yet the "Student List-Students Win" movement attracted anti-government voters across Serbian society.

They fielded candidates for all 250 parliamentary seats, and yet no students were among them.

As he joined the students marching towards Belgrade last week, lead candidate and cardiologist Ilija Srdanović said history was being rewritten: "The energy is unstoppable."

"We offer our citizens the core values of civilised society, which this previous regime has taken away from our citizens for the last time," he told the BBC.

It all began on 1 November 2024, when the concrete canopy collapsed outside Novi Sad train station, in Serbia's second biggest city, killing 16 people.

The tragedy was seen as emblematic of widespread corruption. Critics linked the station's fatally flawed renovation to a president who had closely associated himself with the project.

"When the canopy collapsed that served as the last straw," says Helena Ivanov of the think tank the Henry Jackson Society.

It was an emotional moment that triggered a spark and a national campaign of marches and events, she said, that captured the hearts and minds of Serbians in a way no opposition party had been able to do.

Serbia's veteran ruler Vučić concedes election to student-led protest movement

Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election

From protests to direct challenge to Vučić

What started as weekly student protests demanding justice on university campuses and city streets soon became a national movement, often at a local level, that encompassed far more sections of Serbian society, including farmers, actors and judges.

Vučić's SNS was clearly shaken and by January 2025 his prime minister had resigned "to defuse tensions". In March 2025 Belgrade saw Serbia's biggest ever anti-government protest and as the leaderless student movement increased in strength, they organised themselves through student assemblies or plenums.

By the time Vučić had announced snap elections last month, they were ready. "They have been able to take that emotional momentum into a proper organisation and have people learn how to protect fairness at polling stations," Helena Ivanov explained.

"The message was clear: the rule of law and not ruled by the law," said Gordana Delić, head of the Balkans programme at the German Marshall Fund of the US, who said Sunday's vote was in effect a referendum.

Initially Vučić sought to praise the protesters as "well-intentioned", but ahead of the elections he accused them of trying to "bring down" Serbia. Even after conceding victory on Sunday night he made the unfounded allegation that they had the support of unnamed "European countries and the American deep state".

One thing is clear, it will not be the students, as they were not standing for election. That was a calculated decision as the electorate would probably not voted for a list of candidates with little life experience.

Although their top candidate was Ilija Srdanović, a cardiology professor in Novi Sad, he is not really seen as a likely prime minister.

Few candidates stand out as potential leaders.

According to independent polling group CeSID, 140 people on the list have won seats in parliament, and they include ex-basketball star Dejan Bodiroga (24th on the list), renowned actor Tihomir Stanić (8th), opera singer Nikola Mikić (46th), former National Bank of Serbia governor Dejan Šoškić (27th), and a rather large number of professors.

Šoškić's name has been mentioned in connection with the top post. He has spoken out about reforms he would make to the economy, and he has been widely criticised in pro-government media.

The elected MPs will have the task of fulfilling what is in effect a manifesto.

In the words of the students themselves, they were looking for people who could enter institutions "do their jobs responsibly and not forget why they are there".

Under an 11-point programme, the student movement wants to:

Eradicate corruption by forming a police unit to arrest those responsible for it

Purge officials in the internal affairs ministry of anyone who broke rules on cracking down on protesters, or anyone linked to organised crime

Reform Serbia's skewed media scene and free the public broadcaster of political control

Stop recruiting party loyalists to head public enterprises.

Vučić and the SNS party deny corruption and seeking to influence the media.

Will it still be a student movement, without students?

Although they have not been elected, it is the students who have made the promises to the Serbian people and they will come under pressure to follow through on their manifesto.

The ordinary Serbian citizens they chose to represent their movement have "been entrusted with transferring part of the struggle we have been waging on the streets for the past year into the institutions", the students say.

In his speech on Sunday evening, Vučić told party supporters that the students had destroyed two years of life in Serbia and they would be defeated "faster than they think".

articles.title: A Texas billionaire couple bought a 40,000-acre Nebraska ranch for $56 million; the property has a history of prominent owners, and its new owners want to build a major cattle operation
articles.summary: A Texas billionaire couple has bought a roughly 40,000-acre Nebraska ranch for $56 million, in what appears to be a record-high ranch sale in the state.
articles.body: A Texas billionaire couple has bought a roughly 40,000-acre Nebraska ranch for $56 million, in what appears to be a record-high ranch sale in the state. Mark and Robyn Jones, founders of insurance brokerage Goosehead Insurance, acquired Pawnee Springs Ranch in Lincoln County, a property with a history of prominent owners, including former Nebraska governor Keith Neville and businessman Peter Kiewit. According to the Nebraska Examiner, the couple plans to maintain the ranch’s existing cattle and agricultural operations while developing a “world-class cattle operation” over several years. The purchase also reflects their wider investment interests, with plans to explore further acquisitions across Nebraska, Kansas, Wyoming and Montana.What makes the $56 million Nebraska ranch ideal for cattle productionPawnee Springs Ranch is located in Lincoln County, east of North Platte, and extends from the North Platte River north into Nebraska's Sandhills. The property has nearly six miles of river frontage, nine centre pivots covering approximately 1,700 irrigated acres, calf backgrounding facilities with concrete feed bunks and an indoor-outdoor arena. Its landscape includes fertile river-bottom land and native Sandhills rangeland, which also provides habitat for deer, turkey and waterfowl.Mark Johnson of Hall and Hall, the agricultural real estate company that represented both parties in the transaction, described the property as exemplifying the top qualities of a Nebraska Sandhills river ranch. The ranch already has approximately 2,500 mother cows, alongside its irrigation infrastructure, grassland and river corridors. Mark Jones told the Nebraska Examiner that he wanted an operation focused on “actual agricultural production”, with the property's existing resources supporting the couple's plans for beef production.What is the history of Nebraska’s Pawnee Springs RanchPawnee Springs Ranch has a history dating back to 1918, and its previous owners include former Nebraska governor Keith Neville and construction businessman Peter Kiewit. Kiewit purchased the operation in 1949. He once told the North Platte Telegraph that the ranch took its name from the natural springs that flowed through the area.The Gottsch family became involved with the ranch in 1985, initially leasing the property before eventually purchasing it. The family subsequently operated it as part of its wider agricultural business, which has interests across Nebraska, Kansas, Missouri and Texas. In a statement following the sale, the Gottsches said the ranch had been part of their family for 41 years and recalled three generations participating in spring branding, summer grazing and autumn and winter calf backgrounding. They also thanked the Boeshart family caretakers and neighbouring ranchers who helped during branding season.What are the new owners’ plans for Pawnee Springs RanchThe new owners intend to retain the ranch's existing agricultural activities while building a larger beef production business over several years. Ryan Langston, Mark Jones's son-in-law and the ranch's new chief executive, said the property would largely continue its current work, including raising calves from birth until weaning and returning them to grass as yearlings. The operation will also continue running its agricultural irrigation pivots.The transition will include retaining the three cowboys who currently live and work on the property. Langston said a new manager would be recruited to replace the existing manager, who is leaving with the Gottsch family. He also described the purchase as a “long-term commitment to the area” and said the owners intended to hire local workers where possible, work with neighbouring landowners and contribute to the local community. The couple does not plan to live in Nebraska but expects to maintain an active presence in the area.How did Mark and Robyn Jones build their $2 billion fortuneMark and Robyn Jones built their fortune through their involvement in Goosehead Insurance, the publicly traded insurance brokerage they founded and developed together. The company connects customers with providers of home, motor, flood and other insurance products. The couple continues to serve as its chair and vice-chair, respectively. Forbes estimated their combined net worth at $2 billion, with Robyn Jones also appearing on its 2025 list of America's richest self-made women entrepreneurs.The Nebraska purchase follows their acquisition of Flathead Ridge Ranch in Montana in 2021, a 125,000-acre property that the couple describes as a family legacy investment. Their approach to that ranch has focused on conservation, forest restoration and maintaining public recreational access across most of the property. By contrast, Pawnee Springs Ranch is intended to serve as a commercial agricultural enterprise. Mark Jones told the Nebraska Examiner that the Nebraska operation “will be a platform we can build on”, with the couple looking towards further investments in Nebraska, Kansas, Wyoming and Montana. He also said the opportunity for their grandchildren to work on the ranch was an important attraction of the purchase.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Did US officials campaign to tilt Brazil polls towards Bolsonaros?
articles.summary: Two US state department officials led a campaign to restore Brazil’s right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power and pushed sanctions intended to tilt the
articles.body: Two US state department officials led a campaign to restore Brazil’s right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power and pushed sanctions intended to tilt the presidential election in its favour, according to 10 current and former US officials with direct knowledge of the matter. Senator Flavio Bolsonaro was facing leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a tight run-off Sunday.The officials were Darren Beattie, senior adviser for Western Hemisphere Affairs overseeing Brazil policy, and Ricardo Pita, another senior adviser promoted this year to deputy assistant secretary for North America. Reuters could not determine whether they acted on orders from White House or secretary of state Marco Rubio. President Trump, a defender of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has not publicly endorsed any Brazilian candidate.Before campaigning began, Beattie and Pita told US diplomats that Washington’s policy was to restore Jair Bolsonaro as Brazil’s leader, although he had been disqualified from office for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to Lula, three sources said. After Bolsonaro received a 27-year sentence in Sept 2025, they shifted support to his son Flavio and instructed embassy staff not to engage with rival conservative contenders, the sources said.Since last year, the officials have advocated punitive measures designed to weaken Lula and boost the Bolsonaros, the 10 sources said. These included designating Brazil’s leading gangs, Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV), as terrorist organisations and sanctioning Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who led investigations into Jair Bolsonaro.State department spokesman Tommy Pigott did not address questions about Beattie and Pita but said: “All actions taken by US against narco-traffickers and to protect free speech are to defend the rights and lives of the American people. The Brazilian people have the right to choose their leaders through free and fair elections.” White House declined to comment, while Lula’s office did not respond to requests.Orna Blum, who led state department’s Brazil and Southern Cone office until retiring last year over opposition to Trump administration, said Washington had the right to pursue its interests but added: “But when American foreign policy instruments are used to pressure another democracy over the legal fate of a political ally, the line between diplomacy and political intervention has been crossed.”Beattie is a former White House speechwriter fired in 2018 after addressing an event frequented by white nationalists. He developed “free speech diplomacy”, aimed at punishing countries accused of censoring right-wing speech. Washington accused Moraes of violating free-speech rights by jailing Brazilians over political social-media posts and censoring US platforms. Moraes, who did not respond to Reuters, has said he was combating fake news that undermined faith in democratic institutions.In early 2025, the Bolsonaro family lobbied for sanctions against Moraes under Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act. Jair Bolsonaro’s younger son Eduardo visited Beattie in Washington around April, two former officials said. Beattie then appealed to treasury department’s office of foreign assets control for sanctions, a former official said. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent offered no opposition, the official said. Sanctions were imposed in July 2025 over alleged free-speech violations.Pita also asked sanctions officials to explore terrorist designations for PCC and CV after joining a US delegation that visited Jair Bolsonaro in Brasilia in May 2025. In May 2026, Flavio met Beattie and deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau in Washington to discuss the designations. State department announced them the next day, though Reuters could not establish Beattie or Pita’s influence on the final decision.In July 2025, Washington revoked eight Supreme Court justices’ visas and imposed 50% tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing Bolsonaro’s “persecution”. Analysts said court measures failed to stop his trial and tariffs boosted Lula’s ratings. Washington later diluted tariffs, removed Moraes from sanctions list in December and Brazil barred Beattie from visiting Bolsonaro in prison in March. Trump called Flavio’s narrow first-round lead over Lula a “big victory”.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Ferritin face: Can you really diagnose low iron from your looks?
articles.summary: Videos in which people claim to spot the signs of low iron have attracted millions of views online.
articles.body:
"Do you have ferritin face?" a young woman asks on TikTok, pointing to dark circles, washed-out skin and brittle hair, alongside before-and-after style photographs. The content creator puts these features down to her iron levels.

It is one of a growing number of videos and posts on TikTok and Instagram claiming that low ferritin - a protein which stores iron in the body - can leave visible clues on your face.

Users list pale or grey-looking skin, dark under-eye circles, dry or cracked lips, hair shedding and weak nails, while others share portraits claiming stark visual differences.

The phrase "ferritin face" has spread widely across social media, with videos attracting millions of views.

But doctors say appearance alone cannot diagnose iron deficiency.

"Ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis," said GP Dr Aziza Sesay, who is based in the West Midlands. "However, it may be a clue to tell us that something is going on."

Pale skin, hair shedding or brittle nails can accompany low iron, but can also be signs of other conditions, she told BBC News.

Your ferritin levels show how good your body's iron stores are, while haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells which carries oxygen. When haemoglobin is low, the blood cannot carry as much oxygen - a condition known as anaemia.

But iron stores can become depleted before that happens, meaning someone can be iron-deficient and have symptoms without being anaemic.

"You've got no stored iron but you're maintaining your haemoglobin. That's the big disconnect," said consultant haematologist Dr Drew Provan.

Dr Sue Pavord, also a consultant haematologist, said iron deficiency is common and often under-diagnosed in women.

UK guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology say ferritin below 15 micrograms per litre indicates absent iron stores, while below 30 generally indicates low iron stores.

Lucy M, 32, who posts about hair loss as @marvluceskin on Instagram and TikTok, said "ferritin face" seemed to describe changes she had noticed in herself.

In 2021 she developed heart palpitations, fatigue and hair loss. After being told her blood tests were normal and being diagnosed with generalised anxiety disorder, a later test showed her ferritin was 12 micrograms per litre.

Lucy said she looked "grey" and her hair had become dull and brittle.

She shared photographs with the BBC from when her ferritin was low, compared to when it had recovered, and said the difference between how she felt and looked was "night and day".

Videos about "ferritin face" often encourage viewers to look for a combination of physical signs - from dark circles and pale skin to dry lips, thinning hair and brittle nails - and compare them with their own appearance.

"You're not ugly, your ferritin is low", one creator says, pointing to the camera.

Provan said it was "impossible" to determine someone's ferritin levels from how their face looks.

People who are significantly anaemic may look pale, he explained, while fatigue can contribute to dark circles, but these visual signs are "subjective and unreliable".

In people with darker skin, changes in skin colour may be less obvious, Sesay added, meaning someone looking specifically for the signs described online could miss iron deficiency.

For doctors, symptoms and how someone feels are more useful than appearance.

Blood tests matter not only to confirm iron deficiency, Provan and Sesay said, but to establish the cause and guide treatment.

Both said treatment should also address the cause. Heavy periods, low dietary iron, gastrointestinal blood loss and problems absorbing iron through the gut can all play a role.

Iron deficiency is commonly treated with oral iron. Pavord said iron tablets are best taken on an empty stomach, ideally first thing in the morning, and advised avoiding tea or coffee around the time they are taken because they can inhibit iron absorption.

Iron can also be obtained naturally from foods including meat, beans, lentils, leafy green vegetables and fortified cereals.

Taking iron supplements without a diagnosis can be harmful, while self-treating could delay the investigation of an underlying problem.

Lucy said social media has nevertheless helped women take symptoms more seriously, and has given some the confidence to ask questions when something feels wrong.

"There are so many women saying, 'Oh my gosh, this is me," she said, adding that she is not a doctor and presents her content as her own experience.

For her, doing so has been empowering - giving women information with which to advocate for themselves.

Sesay called social media a "double-edged sword" - it can encourage people to seek help, but can also lead them to incorrectly diagnose themselves from a short video.

For Lucy, the useful part is not diagnosing yourself from your appearance, but knowing when something doesn't feel right, and when to ask questions.

articles.title: Crowded House singer Neil Finn paid a reported NZ$4.2 million for Auckland’s Edinburgh Castle pub; he plans to turn it into a wellness retreat
articles.summary: Neil Finn, the singer-songwriter known for Crowded House and Split Enz, has bought a troubled Auckland pub with plans to give the historic property a new
articles.body: Neil Finn, the singer-songwriter known for Crowded House and Split Enz, has bought a troubled Auckland pub with plans to give the historic property a new purpose. Finn paid a reported NZ$4.2 million for the Edinburgh Castle on Symonds Street in Eden Terrace, according to OneRoof. The off-market deal was completed in March 2026, with the purchase price reportedly NZ$2 million above the property’s rateable value. Built in the 1860s, the pub has faced years of complaints about disorder and violence. It surrendered its liquor licence in 2023 after residents and police opposed its renewal, and it later lost its gambling machine licence in November 2025. Finn’s spokesperson confirmed that he intends to turn the venue into a wellness retreat, although work will begin only after planning permissions are approved. The property is also near Roundhead, Finn’s recording studio, adding another building to his holdings in the neighbourhood.Neil Finn buys Edinburgh Castle pub in Eden Terrace for NZ$4.2 millionThe acquisition became public in May 2026, when The Spinoff reported that Finn had bought the Edinburgh Castle and intended to transform it into a wellness retreat. A spokesperson confirmed the purchase, saying the project would begin once planning permissions were approved. No further details were provided about the proposed facilities, services or opening date. According to OneRoof, the off-market transaction was completed in March 2026, with Finn reportedly paying NZ$4.2 million, around NZ$2 million above the property’s rateable valueThe pub stands on the corner of Symonds Street and Newton Road in Auckland’s Eden Terrace neighbourhood. Finn already owns Roundhead, his recording studio on Newton Road, and has acquired other properties in the surrounding area over the years. Local business owners have welcomed the proposed change. Chand Sahrawat, who operates The French Cafe nearby, told Radio New Zealand that she was excited about Finn taking over the property. She described a concept focused on wellbeing and connection as a welcome change for a site that has faced challenges over the years. The proposed retreat would give the building a different role in the neighbourhood, although its eventual design and operating model remain unclear.Edinburgh Castle pub history: licensing disputes and gambling venue troublesThe Edinburgh Castle dates to the 1860s and is described by The Spinoff as the only surviving hotel from a group built near the top of Symonds Street during that period. Its history of licensing disputes began early. In 1865, 60 residents reportedly opposed granting the hotel a licence, arguing that a hotel was not needed in the area and could disturb the neighbourhood. Despite their objections, the licence was granted. More than a century later, the pub again faced opposition from residents and police over concerns about disorder and violence. According to The Spinoff, the Edinburgh Castle surrendered its liquor licence in 2023 after its renewal was strongly opposed by locals and police. It continued operating as a hotel and gambling venue, including offering accommodation and poker machines.The venue’s later history included the fatal assault on mixed martial arts fighter Fau Vake in May 2021. According to The New Zealand Herald, Vake was punched in the head during a verbal altercation outside the pub and died days later. The four men involved in the case had different legal outcomes. Daniel Havili pleaded guilty to manslaughter and was sentenced to 2 years and 9 months in prison. Ofa Folau received 6 months of home detention for assault, while Siofilisi Paongo received 5 months of home detention for assault-related offences. Neither Folau nor Paongo was responsible for the blows that caused Vake’s death. The fourth man, Semisie Pomale, was discharged without conviction. The individual outcomes are documented in reporting by RNZ, the Otago Daily Times and Newstalk ZB.The pub continued operating after surrendering its liquor licence, but its gambling machine licence ended on November 30, 2025, according to The Spinoff. That removed a major source of revenue from the venue. By the time Finn’s purchase was announced, the building had quietly shut, with plywood covering its entrance. Finn’s plan represents a possible new use for the site, but the proposed retreat remains subject to planning approval. Details about the centre’s facilities and opening date have not been announced.Neil Finn’s Auckland property portfolio: Roundhead and neighbouring purchasesThe Edinburgh Castle purchase adds to Finn’s property holdings around Eden Terrace. OneRoof reported that Finn has acquired buildings on the block since 2003, including a property bought for NZ$1.13 million in 2010. The block houses Roundhead, his recording studio, which has operated in the neighbourhood for more than 20 years. The studio has hosted musicians including Kanye West, Johnny Marr and KT Tunstall, as well as Crowded House and Finn’s son, Liam Finn. The pub and studio are close to one another, giving the acquisition a direct connection to Finn’s existing presence in the area.OneRoof also reported that Finn paid NZ$1.8 million in March 2026 for a neighbouring former panel-beating workshop on Randolph Street. The property measures 440 square metres. The purchase, alongside the Edinburgh Castle deal, adds to his commercial holdings in the neighbourhood. Away from central Auckland, Finn bought a bach in West Auckland in 2021 for more than NZ$3 million, according to OneRoof. The outlet reported that the price was more than double the property’s rateable value at the time.Finn previously owned a villa on Corunna Avenue in Auckland’s Parnell suburb. The property, described as about a century old, sold in 2015 for NZ$3.8 million, according to property reporting by OneRoof and The New Zealand Herald. For now, the Edinburgh Castle’s future depends on the planning process. Finn’s purchase and stated intention to create a wellness retreat have been reported, but the centre’s design, services and opening date have not yet been announced. The project could give a long-troubled venue a new purpose while expanding Finn’s property presence around his recording studio.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth presidential term after defeating conservative challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth presidential term after defeating conservative challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday’s runoff election, with the electoral authority confirming his victory and extending left-wing leadership in Latin America’s largest economy.Addressing supporters in São Paulo after his re-election, Lula said, “BRAZIL IS NO ONE'S BACKYARD,” in an apparent swipe at US influence in the region, after defeating Flávio Bolsonaro, who had advocated closer ties with the Trump administration. He also called for the regulation of digital platforms, claiming Brazil had defeated foreign intervention through them.“We need to regulate digital platforms,” Lula said, adding that his campaign had managed to counter foreign interference through digital platforms.With more than 78% of votes counted, Lula was leading with 51.21% against Bolsonaro’s 48.79%, according to Reuters’ live election coverage. Pollster Datafolha had projected Lula’s victory before the electoral authority officially confirmed the result.Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro called for Brazil's election results to be 'annulled' after Lula da Silva.The victory marks a setback for US President Donald Trump’s allies in Latin America. Flávio Bolsonaro, a senator and son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, had campaigned on strengthening ties with Washington and securing better trade deals with the Trump administration.Lula, who previously governed Brazil from 2003 to 2010, had criticised US tariffs on Brazilian exports and Washington’s designation of drug-trafficking groups as foreign terrorist organisations.Lula calls for broader public participationIn his victory speech, Lula pledged to work with Brazil’s conservative-led Congress, despite political differences, and said he would govern for the entire country.“I will govern for 215 million Brazilians, we no longer have an electoral rival,” Lula said, seeking to strike a conciliatory note after a closely contested campaign that deepened political divisions.He also promised changes to the country’s governance and greater public involvement in policymaking.“We will change the way we run this country, we will make people participate more in decision-making process,” he said.Lula said his campaign had convinced voters that participating in the election was essential to protecting Brazil’s democratic institutions.“We managed to convince people that voting was extremely important to safeguard democracy in Brazil,” he said.The election pitted two sharply polarised political camps against each other, with the campaign dominated by disagreements over relations with the United States, crime, climate policy and social welfare.Lula’s victory gives Brazil and Mexico left-of-centre leadership in two of Latin America’s largest economies, while dealing a setback to conservative forces seeking closer alignment with Trump’s administration.Cost of living, crime shape campaignLula faced a challenging re-election battle amid voter concerns over the cost of living and crime. Bolsonaro made a tough-on-crime agenda central to his campaign and promised to reduce food prices, while Lula offered financial incentives to attract undecided voters.Both political camps were also dogged by corruption allegations involving allies and family members. Bolsonaro faced scrutiny over a sprawling scandal, while Lula had previously spent more than a year in prison following corruption convictions that were later annulled.The runoff was a rematch between two political forces that have divided Brazil in recent years. In the previous presidential election, Lula defeated Jair Bolsonaro by the narrowest margin since the country’s return to democracy in 1985.Flávio Bolsonaro had led Lula by more than 2.2 million votes in the first round earlier this month, setting the stage for a closely fought runoff.Lula’s supporters backed him for his record on poverty reduction and support for marginalised communities. Bolsonaro’s supporters, meanwhile, pointed to high prices and taxes and accused Lula’s political camp of corruption.Trump administration looms over tiesUS policy towards Brazil emerged as a major issue during the campaign, with Lula criticising Trump’s trade measures and approach to tackling organised crime.Flávio Bolsonaro emphasised his links with the White House and argued that Brazil needed better deals with the Trump administration, including in the rare-earth minerals sector. Brazil estimates that it holds deposits of up to 21 million tonnes of rare-earth resources, second only to China.Bolsonaro denied receiving assistance from the US government.Trump said on Sunday that he was following the Brazilian election but declined to endorse either candidate.Lula’s re-election is expected to keep disagreements over trade, US influence and regional diplomacy at the centre of relations between Brasília and Washington.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Microsoft has withdrawn from a major UK data centre deal.
articles.body: Microsoft has withdrawn from a major UK data centre deal. The decision is a setback for British AI infrastructure developer Nscale, which had planned to make its Loughton, Essex, facility operational next year. The project has faced repeated delays, with electricity grid operators reportedly saying power won't be available until the 2030s. Microsoft had agreed to lease 23,000 Nvidia AI chips at the site and was expected to become its anchor tenant.​According to a report by The Telegraph, the withdrawal also comes as Nscale prepares for a potential US stock market listing that could value the company at up to $35 billion (£26 billion), raising questions about its expansion plans and investor confidence in AI infrastructure businesses.​Microsoft withdraws from Nscale's Essex data centre project​Microsoft recently informed Nscale that it was pulling out of the agreement announced last year. The deal was part of Microsoft's broader UK investment commitments worth £22 billion, announced during US President Donald Trump's visit to the country.​The proposed facility would have housed thousands of high-performance Nvidia AI chips. However, difficulties securing electricity connections have delayed the project, forcing Nscale to look for alternative energy sources and new expansion locations.​An Nscale spokesman said: “We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK, and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK. Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term, and this unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts.”​Microsoft did not comment on the decision.​Nscale's planned IPO faces fresh challenges​The setback comes as Nscale considers raising billions of dollars through a potential Wall Street listing. Backed by Nvidia and other investors, the company has been privately valued at $15 billion and reportedly targets a valuation of up to $35 billion through the proposed flotation.​Microsoft accounts for more than 40% of Nscale's $103 billion in contracted revenue, although the Essex project is believed to represent only a small portion of that amount. Anthropic is another major customer.​Long-term commitments from major technology companies matter for data centre developers, which need substantial financing to build facilities and buy computing hardware. Losing Microsoft's commitment to the Essex site could complicate Nscale's efforts to show it can deliver planned infrastructure projects.​Electricity shortages delay Britain's AI infrastructure plans​The Loughton case study highlights challenges in developing the country's AI infrastructure, including the high cost of electricity and long delays in grid connections.​Nscale has also encountered delays at a data centre project in Norway, reportedly resulting in significant penalties. Separately, OpenAI suspended plans in April for a Stargate AI facility with Nscale on Tyneside, citing Britain's high electricity prices.​The wider AI infrastructure sector has faced investor concerns over rising borrowing costs and whether demand will justify the substantial spending required to build data centres. Australian rival Firmus cancelled plans for a $20 billion IPO earlier this month, citing market conditions, while other infrastructure providers have also experienced pressure on their shares and bonds.​Nscale, founded by Australian entrepreneur Josh Payne two years ago, continues to pursue its UK expansion plans despite the Essex setback. The project's future will depend partly on whether the company can secure an alternative power supply and find another customer for the facility.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has urged Israelis to vote for the return of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to office, saying that the two leaders must
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has urged Israelis to vote for the return of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to office, saying that the two leaders must “finish the job” against Iran.The appeal came on Sunday, two days before the election, as polls show Netanyahu’s coalition is far short of a majority. In a fresh post on Truth Social, Trump renewed his endorsement of Netanyahu, whom he first backed a week ago. The latest intervention comes after an Axios report that the Israeli prime minister had been pushing the US president to publicly reaffirm his support.The US President wrote, “To the people of Israel, to those who haven’t seen it, I am attaching the Endorsement I gave one week ago to your Prime Minister, Bibi Netanyahu. As everyone is aware, including the enemy, Bibi and I have had a great relationship in winning together.”Trump also linked his appeal directly to the military campaign against Iran, presenting his cooperation with Netanyahu as a shared effort and urging Israelis to consider what he described as the prime minister’s record as an “outstanding Warrior Prime Minister.”“I did the Venezuelan attack, one of the most successful Military Operations in History but, before that, we did Operation Midnight Hammer, stopping the World’s Number One State Sponsor of Terror from obtaining a Nuclear Weapon. Then we did Operation Epic Fury, and Iran now has No Navy, No Air Force, and both their Military and Economy are in shambles, including the fact that Iran’s Inflation is at 301%. The Naval Blockade has precluded them from getting Oil, and two levels of leadership, both Military and otherwise, are gone. When you go to the Polls please remember that Bibi has been an outstanding Warrior Prime Minister!Trump urged Israelis to re-elect Netanyahu, saying the two leaders must continue their campaign against Iran and prevent threats to Israel and the US. “Israel was called The Little Satan, with the United States being called The Big Satan, by some very evil people. There can no longer be the chant heard around the World of “Death to America, Death to Israel,” and there won’t be. Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started! President DONALD J TRUMP”Trump’s latest show of support comes after months of reported differences over the handling of the conflict with Iran. Many media reports had portrayed the US president as frustrated with Netanyahu for allegedly promising a quick victory against Tehran at the start of the year, a result that did not eventually materialise.The relationship also faced reported strains when Washington chose to halt its campaign against Iran and pursue an agreement. Israel was wary that a deal between the sides could undermine its security.Back in June, Israel’s continued strikes in Lebanon frustrated peace talks with Iran, prompting expletive-laden criticism of Netanyahu from Trump. The US president said then that he would “most likely” endorse Netanyahu’s re-election bid, but wanted to see who else was running before making a decision.Despite these reported disagreements, both leaders have continued to insist that they have a good working relationship.Trump has also repeatedly spoke about elections in other countries, departing from the longstanding norm that US presidents do not publicly intervene in the electoral contests of allied nations.You use AI every day. articles.title: US has ‘two very different sets of intelligence reports’: Trump rules out Sunday strikes on Iran
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday ruled out an immediate military strike against Iran, saying Washington had no plans to launch an attack that day, even
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Sunday ruled out an immediate military strike against Iran, saying Washington had no plans to launch an attack that day, even as conflicting intelligence assessments and uncertainty over diplomatic efforts continued to shape the US approach to Tehran."Would I tell you that? But the answer is no. There will not be a strike," Trump told reporters as he departed the White House for a campaign rally in Michigan, responding to a question about whether military action against Iran could take place as soon as Sunday."We have two very different sets of intelligence reports," Trump said, describing the incoming information as "very advanced."The president maintained that Washington was doing "well with Iran," although an unnamed US official told Israeli news channel i24NEWS that Trump was prepared to "shift gears on Iran" and that military strikes no longer appeared to be "a question of if, but of when."The remarks came after Trump presented Tehran with a stark choice between reaching a diplomatic agreement and facing further military action."Do I make a deal with them, or do I finish them off? That's the only question," Trump told Fox News, framing the next phase of the conflict as a choice between negotiations and escalating military operations.Despite ruling out a strike on Sunday, Trump has continued to signal that Washington could pursue further military action if negotiations fail to produce an agreement.Trump claims US controls Strait of HormuzTrump also asserted that American forces had established maritime dominance over the Strait of Hormuz, a key global shipping route and a major point of contention in the conflict with Iran."Remember, we now control the Hormuz Strait. They get nothing. Yes, we get everything." He maintained that commercial activity through the chokepoint had exceeded pre-war levels and described the US Navy's enforcement of a blockade on Iranian ports and shipping as "unbelievable."On Saturday, Trump had suggested that Washington could either launch fresh military strikes or secure a comprehensive agreement with Tehran. He questioned whether Iran would honour any commitments under a potential deal, while arguing that either outcome would amount to an American victory.Control over the Strait of Hormuz remains a central point of friction in the conflict, which erupted in late February following joint US-Israeli strikes. The confrontation has continued despite a ceasefire and a memorandum aimed at securing a final peace agreement.Trump signals Russia-Ukraine peace talksTurning to the war in Eastern Europe, Trump indicated that high-level diplomatic engagements involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine could take place soon."We're going to be having some pretty soon, and I think they both want to make a deal," he said, expressing optimism about the prospects of negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv.Trump did not provide further details about the proposed engagements or specify when the talks would take place.On Brazil's presidential election, the US president refrained from endorsing either candidate, saying his administration was "watching" the race.Trump links European unrest to immigrationTrump also criticised immigration policies in European countries, linking protests and unrest in France, Italy, Belgium and Spain to what he described as inadequate border enforcement.Contrasting the situation in Europe with US border controls, he claimed that the United States had prevented unauthorised crossings over the preceding 18 months."I closed the border. You know that we've had zero infiltration," Trump said, asserting that "zero illegal aliens" had entered the country during that period. He also claimed that previous US administrations had allowed millions of people to enter illegally.Referring to his conversations with French President Emmanuel Macron, Trump said he had previously warned the French leader about the consequences of immigration policies."'You are destroying France. You're letting people come in that hate your country.'" Trump said he had told Macron.He also cited migrant arrivals in Spain as evidence of what he described as wider instability across Europe.Trump accuses Taiwan of taking US chip industryOn semiconductor manufacturing and trade, Trump accused Taiwan of taking over the US chip industry through low-cost production, renewing his criticism of the island's position in the global semiconductor supply chain."They stole our chip business, all of it, 100%, because they made chips at a ridiculous price, and they just pushed them in," Trump said.He argued that stronger executive leadership in Washington could have prevented broader tensions with China over trade and technology.Trump's comments come amid continuing US efforts to strengthen domestic semiconductor manufacturing and address Washington's strategic competition with Beijing.You use AI every day.
